article_briefs.brief: Tata Motors has increased its all‑cash voluntary tender offer for Iveco to 14.40 euro per share, up from 14.10 euro per share, which would value the transaction at 3.91 billion euro if all 271.2 million Iveco common shares are tendered. The acceptance period runs from September 7 to October 26, 2026, with shareholders scheduled to vote on related resolutions at an extraordinary general meeting on October 16. The revised price reflects a 33.47 per cent premium over Iveco's share price on July 17, 2025 and a 6.77 per cent premium over the price on July 29, 2025, and will be funded through an 85 million euro credit facility agreement with MUFG Bank Ltd, GIFT Branch. Tata Motors said the revised offer will not be increased further.

Tata Motors has lodged its “best and final” €14.40‑a‑share bid for Iveco Group, rejecting any higher offer and increasing the consideration from €14.10 to €14.40 a share, which adds about €81 million to the €3.91‑billion transaction. A shareholder vote this week could lower the acceptance threshold from 95 per cent to 80 per cent, with Exor’s 27.06 per cent stake (over 43 per cent of voting rights) already committed, while large minority holders such as Davidson Kempner, Syquant Capital and Petrus Advisers are estimated to own about 20 per cent and will be pivotal to reaching the 80 per cent bar. The offer is set to close on October 26, and if completed the combined entity would generate roughly €21 billion in annual revenue and sell about 5,90,000 vehicles.

Stellantis India, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd (TMPV) and its subsidiary Tata Passenger Electric Mobility Ltd (TPEM) signed a Definitive Agreement on Monday, expanding their partnership into advanced technology and product collaboration. Under the agreement TMPV will give Stellantis access to its advanced product technology and vehicle architecture to develop vehicles for more than 50 global markets, with manufacturing planned at Fiat India Automobiles Private Limited (FIAPL), the 50:50 joint venture between TMPV and Stellantis in Pune. The deal builds on an MoU signed in February 2026 and is aimed at leveraging Tata’s capabilities in India with Stellantis’ global product development and market reach, according to statements from Shailesh Chandra and Tianshu Xin.

Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Stellantis signed a definitive agreement on October 12, 2026 to expand their partnership into advanced vehicle technology and product development. The deal builds on a February 2026 MoU and gives Stellantis access to Tata's vehicle architecture, with product development to target vehicles for more than 50 global markets and manufacturing to be done in India at Fiat India Automobiles Private Limited, a 50:50 joint venture between the two firms. Stellantis will leverage its portfolio of 14 automotive brands and global engineering expertise, while Tata contributes its technology capabilities, aiming to use India's engineering and manufacturing capacity for export plans.

Tata Motors raised its offer for Iveco Group NV by 2% to €14.40 per share on 9 October, describing it as its “best and final” price as the 26 October tender deadline approaches. The revised offer has attracted acceptances for only 28.4% of the shares, while three major shareholders – hedge funds Davidson Kempner, Syquant Capital and activist investor Petrus Advisers – together hold about 20.4% of Iveco’s common shares and have not tendered. The acquisition, announced on 30 July 2025 in an all‑cash deal valued at €3.8 billion ($4.4 billion) and excluding Iveco’s defence business, would give Tata Motors a foothold in Europe and Latin America and create a global commercial‑vehicle business with combined annual revenue of about €21 billion. The €14.40 price represents a 6.77% premium to Iveco’s closing price on 29 July 2025, but the deal remains at risk if the three investors do not tender their roughly 20.4% stake before the deadline.
